Updated model runs and morning observations will refine the exact peak before market resolution.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and supporting models position 27°C as the consensus maximum for Tokyo on September 4 due to a southward-moving frontal system bringing widespread cloud cover, scattered showers, and reduced insolation.** This setup favors modest daytime warming compared with recent days near or above 30°C, aligning with the 53.5% market-implied probability. Ensemble guidance shows limited potential for brief clearing that could push readings to 28°C (25% odds), while stronger rain or persistent northeasterly flow makes 29°C or higher less likely at 20.5%. Traders are weighting the latest model runs showing highs clustering near 26–27°C, with resolution hinging on the final observed peak before midnight JST. Updated JMA guidance and observational data through the evening will refine these probabilities ahead of market close.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from the Hong Kong Observatory indicate a maximum temperature range of 25–30°C for September 4 under northwest winds of 4–5, with periods of cloud cover and scattered showers expected to limit daytime heating. These conditions, influenced by residual tropical cyclone effects and moderate humidity levels around 65–90%, reduce incoming solar radiation and convective mixing, keeping peak readings near or slightly below seasonal averages. Numerical weather models show close agreement on afternoon maxima, but small shifts in shower timing or wind speed could determine whether the daily high reaches 30°C or edges to 31°C. Updated model runs and the next HKO briefing will provide the clearest signals for resolution.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and ensemble forecasts indicate morning marine layer and low clouds over coastal Los Angeles on September 4, with onshore flow limiting afternoon warming and supporting highs near the 1991–2020 average of 76.7 °F. Model consensus clusters around 73–81 °F, but persistent sea-breeze effects and typical early-September climatology favor the lower end of that range, driving the 76–77 °F bin to 61.5 % implied probability. Warmer 78–79 °F and 80–81 °F outcomes receive lower weight because they would require stronger offshore flow or delayed marine-layer clearance, scenarios not currently favored by the latest guidance. Updated NWS point forecasts and afternoon model runs tomorrow will provide the final data traders are monitoring ahead of market resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Esenboğa Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=ltac

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models from multiple sources converge on a daytime high of 29–30°C for Ankara on September 5, 2026, under clear to partly cloudy skies, light northeasterly winds, and negligible precipitation risk.** This places the market-implied probabilities for 29°C (51.5%) and 28°C (29.0%) in line with current guidance, while the 30°C outcome (15.5%) reflects the upper end of the expected range. Ankara’s continental climate typically sees early-September highs near 27°C, so the current pattern sits modestly above the seasonal baseline amid ongoing warm conditions across the region. Stable high pressure and dry air have limited convective activity, keeping temperatures consistent in recent official outlooks. Final model runs and observational updates in the next 48 hours will determine whether any minor cooling or warming adjustments shift the tight clustering around these central outcomes.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from ECMWF and GFS models indicate a ridge of high pressure maintaining clear skies and light westerly flow over the Po Valley, favoring an afternoon maximum near 34–35 °C on September 5 under strong insolation and minimal cloud cover. With resolution imminent, traders are monitoring the next high-resolution runs and official Servizio Meteorologico updates for any last adjustments to the peak value.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader consensus in this short-range temperature market centers on AEMET guidance and high-resolution model runs showing peak Madrid temperatures of 36–38 °C on September 5.** Persistent high pressure supports subsidence and southerly flow that has maintained a heatwave, with recent observations and ensembles indicating afternoon maxima near 37 °C under partly cloudy skies. Increasing mid-level moisture and variable cloud cover are the key variables that could cap insolation and keep readings at or below 36 °C, while clearer conditions or stronger downslope warming would favor 38 °C. Market-implied probabilities around 36–37 °C reflect this narrow uncertainty band two days out, with resolution hinging on the final observed maximum at the Retiro or Barajas reference stations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon activity and widespread thunderstorm development are capping Manila's daytime highs near 28–30°C on September 5, according to the latest model consensus. Heavy cloud cover, high humidity near 90%, and frequent rain reduce solar heating while evaporative cooling and stronger westerly winds further limit afternoon peaks. These conditions align with the rainy-season climatology, where September averages sit around 31°C but drop several degrees under active monsoon flow. Short-term forecast runs show only modest day-to-day variability, keeping the tight clustering between 29°C and 30°C favored by traders, though any delay in storm timing could briefly allow a 31°C reading before renewed convection.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Minister Pistarini Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=saez

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This aligns with trader consensus reflected in the elevated implied probabilities for those exact outcomes, as recent observations show temperatures dropping from the low 20s°C earlier in the week. Historical September averages near 19°C provide context for the below-normal reading, while minor model spread around wind strength and cloud cover introduces limited uncertainty that could allow a 14°C peak if stabilization occurs faster than expected. Updated guidance from official sources will clarify resolution thresholds in the final days.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=mpmg

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from models including GFS and ECMWF point to afternoon convection and scattered thunderstorms over Panama City, Panama, on September 5, likely capping daytime maxima near 29–31 °C amid typical rainy-season humidity above 80 % and light northwest winds. These conditions create narrow differentiation among the closely matched 30 °C, 31 °C, and 32 °C market outcomes, as earlier or heavier showers suppress solar heating while clearer intervals allow brief spikes toward the upper end of the range. Historical September averages near 30 °C provide context, with no unusual large-scale drivers such as strong ENSO signals evident in current observations. Updated model runs and official monitoring closer to the date will refine resolution criteria for the daily maximum.
